Subject: Request: elevated availability target for Polaris P2

Hi Priyom,

Quick note from product/infra at Polaris — we ran a prep PoC last week and things look promising. As we move to pilot, the compliance and ops teams want a written availability target and an operational commitment for high-throughput inference traffic. Specifically they're asking if Redwood can support a 99.99% availability floor (monthly) for our Priority P2 workloads and provide a playbook for failover and escalation.

This is material to our procurement / legal timeline and will feed into the contract we present to the CFO next month. If Redwood can sign to something close to 99.99% (or provide a clear fallback path with defined remediation), we have buy-in to proceed to a 6-month paid pilot at scale.

Can you advise next steps and who at Redwood should weigh in on feasibility and ops? Attaching a short diagram of our expected traffic pattern.

Attachments: polaris-poc-traffic.png (image)

Thanks,

Subject: Polaris request: availability ask (99.99%) — need tech + product assessment

Hi Laura / Marcus —

Polaris (potential strategic pilot, deal DL-2026-457) has asked for a 99.99% monthly availability target for a Priority P2 inference workload. Priyom cc'd the traffic profile. Can you help assess feasibility and operationalizability? A few specific asks: 

- Feasibility: can our runtime + routing + dedicated pool support a contractual 99.99% availability for the expected qps and p95 latency targets?
- Modes: list recommended approaches (reserved Dedicated pool, multi-region failover + model variant fallback, pre-warmed hot-standby).
- Work/cache impact: any data retention, KV cache warmup, or batching tradeoffs we need to call out (particularly for cold-starts during failover).
- Effort estimate: rough dev/ops days and whether this requires roadmap reprioritization (or is doable within current infra runbook).
- Monitoring & SLA mechanics: what metrics we'd report and how incidents are handled (SLA credits, escalation chain).

Polaris is sensitive to timeline (CFO review in ~6 weeks). If we can provide two options (conservative: Dedicated + higher commit with a premium; pragmatic: Best-effort + explicit failover runbook), that will help pricing and legal.

Marcus / Laura — please reply with bullet answers so I can summarize to the Polaris team. If helpful, attach a draft playbook.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2026 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Polaris request: availability ask (99.99%) — need tech + product assessment

Karthik, team —

High level assessment (short bullets):

1) Capability: 99.99% is achievable under a Reserved Dedicated pool model with explicit ingress shaping and hot-standby in a second region. For hosted/multi-tenant variants it is risky to promise 99.99% for sustained high QPS without dedicated capacity.

2) Two recommended options to present to Polaris:
  - Option A (Premium, contract-backed): Dedicated GPU pool in single primary region + hot-standby pool in failover region, pre-warmed caches, prioritized scheduling; provide a monthly availability SLA with defined credit terms. Estimated uplift: +45–60% on token/instance cost in committed pricing. Engineering effort: 6–8w for hardened runbook, capacity reservation automation, and monitoring dashboards.
  - Option B (Operational commitment + fallback): Keep multi-tenant serving but commit to a published failover & escalation playbook (cold-start risks called out), implement prefix/KV cache priming scripts and a scheduled warm-up for expected peak windows. No formal 99.99% contractual credit, but strong operational support and guaranteed 95th–99th percentile runbook response. Lower cost; engineering effort: 2–3w to codify runbook and monitoring hooks.

3) Technical notes / caveats:
  - Cold-starts: warming KV caches is effective but not instantaneous; expect brief windows where p95 degrades during region failover.
  - Model variants: using a quantized variant in failover can reduce latency but may affect output fidelity; include evaluation in pilot acceptance criteria.
  - Monitoring: need to expose token-level latency and request-failure rates to Polaris (dashboard + routed alerts).

4) Runbook & artifacts: attached draft "availability-elevation-playbook-v1.md" and a pricing sketch in "polaris-availability-proposal-v1.pdf". Both are preliminary.

Recommendation: present both options to Polaris, highlight tradeoffs, and push for Option A if they need contractual recourse. If Polaris prefers Option B, we should tie acceptance tests and warm-up windows into the contract to reduce ambiguity.

If you want, Marcus can add a short engineering note on the cache priming approach.

— Laura
VP Product (Serving), Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: availability-elevation-playbook-v1.md (draft), polaris-availability-proposal-v1.pdf (pricing sketch)

- Option B (Operational playbook): No contractual 99.99% guarantee, but strong operational commitments, cache-priming, and runbook with guaranteed SLT response times. Lower cost.
